user.title: Power Insight
user.description:
Power Insight shows where your home's power comes from, where it goes, and what it costs and saves you.

Name this setup to begin. Afterwards, use **Add device** to add your grid connection, PV systems, batteries and consumers.

data_description.name: For example "Home". Used as the prefix of every device and sensor name.

preset.title: Choose your sensors
preset.description: Pick a starting set of sensors. You can change it at any time in the integration's **Options**.

data_description.preset:
**Minimal** — power split in %, where each consumer's power comes from, and financial return.
**Recommended** — adds the power split in W, battery charging sources, and running totals for costs, savings and export compensation. Best for most homes.
**Extended** — adds live cost, savings and export compensation rates (per hour) and each device's share of the home totals.

abort.already_configured: Power Insight is already set up.

init.title: Power Insight options
init.description:
Pick a sensor set for all devices, or **Custom** to choose sensors per device type on the following pages.

Sensors you turn off are disabled, not deleted — their history is kept.

data_description.preset:
**Minimal** — power split in %, consumer power sources, financial return.
**Recommended** — adds power split in W, battery charging sources, and running totals.
**Extended** — adds live rates (per hour) and each device's share of the home totals.
**Custom** — choose per device type.
data_description.debug_power_entities: Adds diagnostic sensors with the raw values used in the calculations. Leave off unless troubleshooting.

combined.title: Combined sensors
combined.description: Sensors for your **whole home**, on the *Combined* device.

data_description.distribution_power: *Home consumption power*, *Battery charging power* and *System standby power*.
data_description.distribution_ratios: The same split as a percentage of all power entering the home, plus the *Export ratio*.
data_description.home_base_load: Adds a device for everything your home uses that has no sensor of its own (total home consumption minus your consumers). Shows its power, where it came from, and what it saved.

data_description.cost_method:
**None** — no cost sensors.
**Standard** — priced at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — priced at each device's lifetime cost per kWh (LCOE/LCOS). Needs the lifetime cost and production of each device.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_costs: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.savings_method:
Money you did not pay the grid because your own devices supplied the power.

**None** — no savings sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — net of each device's lifetime cost per kWh. Needs the lifetime cost and production of each device.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_savings: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.financial_return_method:
Savings plus export compensation, across all devices.

**None** — no financial return sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price.
**Levelized** — net of each device's lifetime cost per kWh. Needs the lifetime cost and production of each device.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_financial_return: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

grid.title: Grid sensors
grid.description: Sensors for your **grid connection**: what you import and export, and what it costs and earns.

data_description.distribution_power: *Import power*, *Export power*, and where the import goes: *Import to home consumption*, *to batteries*, *to system standby*.
data_description.distribution_ratios: Where the import goes, as a percentage of the import.
data_description.distribution_shares: How much of the home's consumption, battery charging and system standby the grid supplies.

data_description.export_compensation_rate: What your home currently earns per hour from exports.
data_description.export_compensation_total: Running total of the export compensation earned.

data_description.cost_method:
**None** — no cost sensors.
**Standard** — *Import cost rate*: the import priced at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
data_description.accumulate_costs: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

pv_system.title: PV system sensors
pv_system.description: Sensors for each **PV system**: where its power goes, and what it costs, saves and earns. These settings apply to all PV systems.

data_description.distribution_power: Where the production goes: *Production to home consumption*, *to batteries*, *to system standby*, *to grid*.
data_description.distribution_ratios: The same split, as a percentage of this PV system's production.
data_description.distribution_shares: How much of the home's consumption, battery charging, system standby and export this PV system supplies.

data_description.export_compensation_rate: What this PV system currently earns per hour from exports.
data_description.export_compensation_total: Running total of the export compensation earned.

data_description.cost_method:
*Operating cost*: what the system's own draw costs (e.g. the inverter at night).

**None** — no cost sensors.
**Standard** — priced at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — priced at the lifetime cost per kWh of the devices supplying it. Needs lifetime values.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_costs: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.savings_method:
Money you did not pay the grid because this PV system supplied the power.

**None** — no savings sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — net of this PV system's own LCOE. Needs the system's lifetime cost and production.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_savings: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.financial_return_method:
Savings plus export compensation for this PV system.

**None** — no financial return sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price.
**Levelized** — net of this PV system's own LCOE, so it shows profit. Needs the system's lifetime cost and production.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_financial_return: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

battery.title: Battery sensors
battery.description: Sensors for each **battery**: where its discharge goes, what charges it, and what it costs, saves and earns. These settings apply to all batteries.

data_description.distribution_power: Where the discharge goes: *Discharge to home consumption*, *to batteries*, *to system standby*, *to grid*.
data_description.distribution_ratios: The same split, as a percentage of this battery's discharge.
data_description.distribution_shares: How much of the home's consumption, battery charging, system standby and export this battery supplies.
data_description.charging_source_shares: One sensor per charging source, e.g. *Charging share from PV System*: how much of the battery's charging comes from that source.

data_description.export_compensation_rate: What this battery currently earns per hour from exports.
data_description.export_compensation_total: Running total of the export compensation earned.

data_description.cost_method:
*Operating cost*: what charging the battery costs.

**None** — no cost sensors.
**Standard** — priced at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — priced at the lifetime cost per kWh of the devices supplying it. Needs lifetime values.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_costs: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.savings_method:
Money you did not pay the grid because the battery supplied the power.

**None** — no savings sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — net of this battery's own LCOS. Needs the battery's lifetime cost and discharged energy.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_savings: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.financial_return_method:
Savings plus export compensation, minus what charging cost.

**None** — no financial return sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price.
**Levelized** — net of this battery's own LCOS, so it shows profit. Needs the battery's lifetime cost and discharged energy.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_financial_return: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

consumer.title: Consumer sensors
consumer.description: Sensors for each **consumer** (e.g. heat pump, EV charger): where its power comes from and what it costs. These settings apply to all consumers.

data_description.power_source_shares: One sensor per source, e.g. *Power share from PV System*: how much of the consumer's power comes from that source.
data_description.distribution_shares: The consumer's share of the home's total consumption.

data_description.cost_method:
*Operating cost*: what running the consumer costs, based on where its power comes from.

**None** — no cost sensors.
**Standard** — priced at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
**Levelized** — priced at each source's lifetime cost per kWh. Needs lifetime values on your PV systems and batteries.
**Both** — one sensor for each method.
data_description.accumulate_costs: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

data_description.savings_method:
*Avoided cost*: what the consumer did not pay the grid because your own devices supplied it. The producing devices report the same money as their savings — don't add the two.

**None** — no savings sensors.
**Standard** — valued at the live grid price. Needs an electricity price sensor on your grid connection.
data_description.accumulate_savings: Adds running totals that keep counting across restarts.

error.reconfigure_adapters_first: These devices are missing values the selected sensors need: {adapters_needing_reconfigure}. Open **Reconfigure** on each device to add them (e.g. a price sensor for costs, lifetime values for levelized sensors), then save again.

user.title: Add device
user.description: What do you want to add?

configure.title: Add {adapter_type}
configure.description: Which fields are required depends on the sensors you enabled in the options.

data_description.name: For example "Rooftop" or "Heat pump". Used in the device and sensor names.
data_description.power_entity:
Sensor with this device's power in W, kW or MW.
Grid: positive = import, negative = export.
PV system and battery: positive = producing or discharging, negative = drawing or charging.
Consumer: negative = drawing. Most plugs report their draw as positive — then turn on **Invert power sign**.
data_description.power_entity_inverted: Turn on if your sensor uses the opposite sign.
data_description.grid_electricity_price_entity: Sensor or number with the current price per kWh you pay for grid power. Required for cost, savings and financial return sensors.
data_description.co2_intensity_entity: Sensor with the grid's current CO₂ intensity in g/kWh (e.g. from Electricity Maps). Optional; reserved for CO₂ sensors.
data_description.exports_power: Turn on if this device can feed power into the grid.
data_description.export_compensation: What you are paid per kWh fed into the grid. Required for savings, financial return and export compensation sensors.
data_description.source_mode:
**Whole mix** — the power comes from all sources in proportion to what they supply.
**Specific devices** — only from the sources you select below, e.g. a battery that charges from solar only.
data_description.charge_from_adapters: The sources this battery charges from. Only used with **Specific devices**.
data_description.power_from_adapters: The sources that power this consumer. Only used with **Specific devices**.
data_description.lifetime_production: Energy in kWh you expect this device to deliver over its lifetime: generated (PV) or discharged (battery). Used for levelized sensors.
data_description.lifetime_cost: Total cost over the device's lifetime (purchase, installation, maintenance). Used for levelized sensors.
data_description.co2_footprint: CO₂ emitted to make and install this device, in kg. Optional; reserved for CO₂ sensors.

abort.grid_already_configured: A grid connection is already set up. Only one is supported.

no_grid_configured.title: {entry_title} needs a grid connection
no_grid_configured.description:
**{entry_title}** has no grid connection, so no costs, savings or power split can be calculated.

Open **Settings → Devices & services → Power Insight**, select **Add device → Grid connection**, and pick the sensor with your grid power (positive = import).

This message disappears once the grid connection is added.

reconfigure_battery_adapters.title: Check the charging sources of {battery_name}
reconfigure_battery_adapters.description: A possible charging source was added or removed. Open **{battery_name}**, choose **Reconfigure**, and check which sources it charges from.

reconfigure_consumer_sources.title: Check the power sources of {device_name}
reconfigure_consumer_sources.description: **{device_name}** is restricted to a power source that has been removed. Open **{device_name}**, choose **Reconfigure**, and check which sources it may draw from.

price_unit.title: The electricity price of {entry_title} has an unknown unit
price_unit.description:
**{entity_id}** reports its price in `{unit}`, which is not a price per unit of energy, so it is ignored and every cost that needs it reads unknown.

Use a price sensor in a unit like `EUR/kWh`, `ct/kWh` or `EUR/MWh` — Power Insight converts those itself — and select it under **Reconfigure** on the grid connection.

price_currency.title: The electricity price of {entry_title} is in another currency
price_currency.description:
**{entity_id}** reports its price in **{currency}**, but Home Assistant is set to **{configured}**. Power Insight does not convert currencies, so every cost is shown in {configured} while being calculated in {currency}.

Use a price sensor in {configured}, or change the currency under **Settings → System → General**.

shared_power_entity.title: Two devices of {entry_title} share a power sensor
shared_power_entity.description:
**{devices}** all read **{entity_id}**. A power sensor measures one device: shared, its watts are counted twice and one of the devices never updates.

Open each device, choose **Reconfigure**, and give it its own power sensor — or remove the one that duplicates another.

metering_imbalance.title: The meters of {entry_title} disagree
metering_imbalance.description:
For the last 15 minutes the metered devices of **{entry_title}** drew {share} more than the grid, PV systems and batteries supplied. Meters sampled at different moments cause brief gaps, which Power Insight evens out; a gap this persistent usually means a misconfigured meter.

Check that every power sensor has the right sign (turn on **Invert** where it reports the opposite way), and that no metered device sits inside another metered circuit, so its power is not counted twice. The **Metering imbalance** diagnostic sensor shows the gap as it happens.

This message disappears once the meters agree again.

set_value.name: Set value
set_value.description: Sets a Power Insight total sensor to a value, e.g. to carry over totals from before you installed it.

migration_downgrade.message: This configuration was saved by a newer version of Power Insight (config version {version}). Reinstall that version or newer, or remove and re-add the integration.

set_value_not_total.message: {entity_id} is not a total sensor. Set value only works on sensors that add up over time.
